-- Pipeline freshness gate: the newest successful load must be recent. This is
-- wall-clock freshness of the pipeline, distinct from event-time freshness
-- (which the GX gate checks against the batch day).
--
-- Runs inside `dbt build`, so a stale or silent pipeline fails the same gate
-- as a bad model.



with latest as (

    select max(loaded_at) as last_loaded_at
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`ops`.`load_audit`
    where status = 'success'

)

select
    last_loaded_at,
    timestamp_diff(current_timestamp(), last_loaded_at, hour) as hours_since_load,
    26 as sla_hours,
    'pipeline is stale' as violation
from latest
where last_loaded_at is null
   or timestamp_diff(current_timestamp(), last_loaded_at, hour) > 26

-- Dedupe keeps the most recent row for a key. Raw is append-only and the
-- loader is idempotent per batch, so this is a safety net for forced reloads
-- and for the deliberate duplicate_pk incident.

with source as (

    select * from `ledgerline-514016`.`raw`.`raw_customers`

),

deduped as (

    select *
    from source
    qualify row_number() over (
        partition by customer_id
        order by created_at desc
    ) = 1

)

    customer_id,
    trim(customer_name) as customer_name,
    lower(trim(email)) as email,
    upper(trim(country)) as country,
    cast(created_at as timestamp) as created_at
from deduped

-- Conformed date dimension. Spans order dates and refund dates so both facts
-- join without nulls; `generate_date_array` is a pure query (no DML), which
-- keeps this compatible with the BigQuery sandbox.

with order_bounds as (

    select min(order_date) as min_day, max(order_date) as max_day
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`staging`.`stg_orders`

),

return_bounds as (

    select min(returned_date) as min_day, max(returned_date) as max_day
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`staging`.`stg_returns`

),

bounds as (

    select
        least(coalesce(o.min_day, r.min_day), coalesce(r.min_day, o.min_day)) as min_day,
        greatest(coalesce(o.max_day, r.max_day), coalesce(r.max_day, o.max_day)) as max_day
    from order_bounds as o
    cross join return_bounds as r

),

spine as (

    select day
    from bounds,
    unnest(generate_date_array(min_day, max_day, interval 1 day)) as day

)

select
    day                                          as date_day,
    extract(year from day)                       as year,
    extract(quarter from day)                    as quarter,
    extract(month from day)                      as month,
    format_date('%B', day)                       as month_name,
    extract(isoweek from day)                    as iso_week,
    extract(dayofweek from day)                  as day_of_week,
    format_date('%A', day)                       as day_name,
    extract(dayofweek from day) in (1, 7)        as is_weekend
from spine

-- Line-grain fact. order_item_key is a deterministic surrogate key because
-- the raw feed has no line id; the composite is unique by generator invariant
-- and is enforced by the raw GX gate.

with items as (

    select * from `ledgerline-514016`.`staging`.`stg_order_items`

),

orders as (

    select order_id, customer_id, order_date
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`staging`.`stg_orders`

)

select
    concat(i.order_id, '|', i.product_id) as order_item_key,
    i.order_id,
    i.product_id,
    o.customer_id,
    o.order_date,
    i.quantity,
    i.unit_price_cents,
    i.amount_cents
from items as i
left join orders as o using (order_id)

-- Order-level financial rollup: one row per order, no fan-out from the
-- one-to-many joins. Facts are built from this so every mart agrees on what
-- an order earned.

with orders as (

    select * from `ledgerline-514016`.`staging`.`stg_orders`

),

items as (

    select
        order_id,
        count(*)            as line_count,
        sum(amount_cents)   as order_total_cents
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`staging`.`stg_order_items`
    group by order_id

),

payments as (

    -- A payment row exists only for paid or refunded orders; `status` records
    -- whether the money was later returned, not whether it was collected.
    select
        order_id,
        sum(amount_cents) as payment_amount_cents
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`staging`.`stg_payments`
    group by order_id

),

refunds as (

    select
        order_id,
        sum(amount_cents) as refunded_cents
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`staging`.`stg_returns`
    group by order_id

)

select
    o.order_id,
    o.customer_id,
    o.order_ts,
    o.order_date,
    o.order_status,
    o.currency,
    coalesce(i.line_count, 0)          as line_count,
    coalesce(i.order_total_cents, 0)   as order_total_cents,
    coalesce(p.payment_amount_cents, 0) as payment_amount_cents,
    coalesce(r.refunded_cents, 0)      as refunded_cents,
    coalesce(p.payment_amount_cents, 0) - coalesce(r.refunded_cents, 0)
        as net_revenue_cents,
    o.order_status = 'cancelled' as is_cancelled,
    o.order_status = 'refunded'  as is_refunded
from orders as o
left join items    as i using (order_id)
left join payments as p using (order_id)
left join refunds  as r using (order_id)

-- Volume anomaly gate: the latest day must be within a band of the trailing
-- 7-day average. A truncated or partially-loaded batch keeps its manifest
-- internally consistent, so only a baseline comparison catches it.
--
-- Empty history (fewer than 2 days) passes: there is nothing to compare to.



with daily as (

    select
        order_date,
        count(*) as orders
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`marts`.`fct_orders`
    group by order_date

),

baseline as (

    select
        order_date,
        orders,
        avg(orders) over (
            order by order_date
            rows between 7 preceding and 1 preceding
        ) as trailing_avg_orders
    from daily

)

select
    order_date,
    orders,
    trailing_avg_orders,
    safe_divide(abs(orders - trailing_avg_orders), trailing_avg_orders) as deviation
from baseline
where trailing_avg_orders is not null
  and safe_divide(abs(orders - trailing_avg_orders), trailing_avg_orders) > 0.3

-- Money is integer cents and must never go negative. A negative amount means
-- a sign error or a malformed refund, not a business event.

with violations as (

    select 'fct_orders.order_total_cents' as check_name, order_id as record_key,
           order_total_cents as value
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`marts`.`fct_orders`
    where order_total_cents < 0

    union all

    select 'fct_orders.payment_amount_cents', order_id, payment_amount_cents
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`marts`.`fct_orders`
    where payment_amount_cents < 0

    union all

    select 'fct_orders.refunded_cents', order_id, refunded_cents
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`marts`.`fct_orders`
    where refunded_cents < 0

    union all

    select 'fct_order_items.amount_cents', order_item_key, amount_cents
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`marts`.`fct_order_items`
    where amount_cents < 0 or unit_price_cents < 0 or quantity <= 0

    union all

    select 'fct_returns.amount_cents', return_id, amount_cents
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`marts`.`fct_returns`
    where amount_cents < 0

)

select * from violations

-- The order header and the payment must agree: for every non-cancelled order
-- the collected amount equals the sum of its lines. This is the test that
-- catches an upstream join fan-out or a duplicated order_items load, which a
-- per-table not-null/unique suite cannot see.

with mismatched as (

    select
        order_id,
        order_total_cents,
        payment_amount_cents,
        order_total_cents - payment_amount_cents as delta_cents
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`marts`.`fct_orders`
    where order_status != 'cancelled'
      and order_total_cents != payment_amount_cents

)

select * from mismatched

-- Refunds cannot exceed the payment they reverse. Also guards the cancelled
-- path, which should carry no payment at all.

with violations as (

    select
        order_id,
        payment_amount_cents,
        refunded_cents,
        'refund exceeds payment' as violation
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`marts`.`fct_orders`
    where refunded_cents > payment_amount_cents

    union all

    select
        order_id,
        payment_amount_cents,
        refunded_cents,
        'cancelled order has a payment' as violation
    from `ledgerline-514016`.`marts`.`fct_orders`
    where order_status = 'cancelled'
      and payment_amount_cents > 0

)

select * from violations
